issues.description: The problem statement text instructs students to implement addGuestStudents(String), but the UML diagram, template TODO, and solution implementation use addGuestStudents(int). This mismatch between the prose and the actual expected signature will confuse students about the correct parameter type.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the parameter type consistent. Update problem_statement.md to instruct implementing addGuestStudents(int) (matching the UML and solution), or if a String parameter was intended, update the template and solution to use addGuestStudents(String) and clarify how to interpret/parse the string. Preferably change the prose to addGuestStudents(int) to match the UML/tests and solution.

issues.description: The problem statement's task description specifies addGuestStudents(String) (text) while the UML in the same problem statement and the solution implementation define addGuestStudents(int). This mismatch in the parameter type for the same method name creates ambiguity for students about the expected signature and input type.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the problem statement and UML consistent with the implementation. Change the textual task description to specify addGuestStudents(int) to match the UML and solution (or alternatively update the UML and solution to use String if that was intended). Prefer aligning the problem text to addGuestStudents(int) to avoid student confusion.
